name: Venkat Suprabath Bitra
tagline: PhD Student in Electrical Engineering, Columbia University
bio: I'm a first-year PhD student in Electrical Engineering at Columbia University, where my work spans audio machine learning, mechanistic interpretability, and embedded computer vision. As a Research Assistant, I'm developing lightweight neural architectures for real-time pitch and voicing estimation and exploring physics-informed neural networks for rule-constrained music generation.

I completed my Master's in Computer Science at Columbia in December 2025, with a thesis on a VAE-based audio encoder paired with a Mamba-enhanced DDSP decoder for music synthesis and timbre transfer. Before Columbia, I completed an Integrated M.Tech in Computer Science at IIIT Bangalore, where my research ranged from moving object segmentation for SLAM to GAN-based 3D face editing and TinyML deployment of spectral analysis models. I've also spent time as a research intern at Adobe Research and the University of British Columbia, and published across venues in signal processing, computer vision, and computational biology.
